name: POST /api/routing-rules - Create a lead routing rule
description: Creates a rule that routes matching leads to a named owner. Rules are evaluated in ascending evaluation_order and the FIRST match wins; a rule with source_channel omitted is a catch-all. Creating a row at the collection root, so it answers 201. Protected - routing configuration decides who owns revenue and is never publicly writable. assigned_user_id must name a real user: a rule pointing at a non-existent owner would route leads into a hole, so the handler answers NOT_FOUND rather than accepting it. QA: depends on register (which creates the user this rule assigns to) and login; the assigned_user_id comes from register's captured user id. MUST-36 note: testCases[2] passes not-a-uuid as assigned_user_id ON PURPOSE - it is the negative case proving the handler rejects a malformed id with 400 before it reaches the database. The happy path DOES resolve assigned_user_id from its producer via register's captured user id, so this is not the var-for-FK antipattern; the static wrapper is what MUST-33 asks for so a deliberate literal is distinguishable from a placeholder somebody forgot. Removing this case would delete the only coverage of that guard.

testCases.name: Create a routing rule for web-form leads
Reject an assigned_user_id that is not a UUID

errorCases.when: name is missing or over 160 characters, assigned_user_id is absent or not a UUID, source_channel is not one of the fourteen channels, criteria is over 255 characters, evaluation_order is not an integer between 0 and 100000, or is_active is not a boolean
the Authorization header is absent, or present without a Bearer token
the bearer token fails verification or has expired
assigned_user_id is a well-formed UUID but no user holds it
